jobs.description:
The Enviva team is driven by our shared vision for a renewable energy future. We are a fast-growing, purpose-driven, global energy company specializing in delivering sustainable wood bioenergy solutions. We are the world’s largest producer of sustainable wood pellets, which provide a low-carbon alternative to fossil fuels.

Introduction

The Enviva team is driven by our shared vision for a renewable energy future. We are a fast-growing, purpose-driven, global energy company specializing in delivering sustainable wood bioenergy solutions. We are the world's largest producer of sustainable wood pellets, providing biogenic carbon solutions for power and heat generation, industrial processes, chemicals, and advanced biofuels worldwide.

Job Purpose

Enviva seeks a motivated and detail-oriented Geospatial Analyst I to join its Sustainability team. Reporting to the Lead Geospatial Specialist, this role will support the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of geospatial data used in forestry operations, supplier traceability, sustainability reporting, and field-to-office workflows.

The position will initially focus on data editing, quality assurance, established workflow execution, and operational GIS support. The successful candidate will be expected to identify recurring data problems, recognize opportunities to replace manual efforts with automation, and suggest practical workflow improvements.

This is an early-career position for someone with a strong GIS foundation who wants to develop their experience in geospatial data management, automation, remote-sensing outputs, and interactive reporting in a fast-moving, innovative department.

Responsibilities

Review geospatial and tabular data for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and adherence to established standards.
Identify, document, and communicate geometry, attribute, identifier, relationship, attachment, and data-model issues via spatial hosted feature services. This will commence with data corrections for review, progressing into assumed responsibility for data quality assurance.
Understand, run, and examine results of established geoprocessing tools, scripts, SQL queries, data updates, and QA/QC checks.
Maintain authoritative tract, stand, supplier, and related operational datasets.
Investigate GIS application and workflow issues, with ability to distinguish incorrect source data, user error, and system flaws.
Provide first-line support for Field Maps and other operational GIS applications, escalating issues when appropriate.
Support supplier-data intake, standardization, validation, and loading into established GIS datasets.
Work with the Sustainability Analyst and operational teams to document, assign, track, and resolve identified data issues.
Support development and maintenance of geospatial error-flagging system for managing discrepancies, corrections, and recurring data-quality trends.
Support changes to field-to-office workflows and help implement attribute rules, validation processes, and data-enrichment methods.
Produce standalone maps and GIS data deliverables upon request.
Identify repetitive manual processes and recommend opportunities for improved efficiency, consistency, or automation.
Document workflows, processing decisions, identified issues, and completed corrections.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, geography, forestry, natural resources, environmental science, civil engineering, information systems, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
Two to four years of relevant GIS experience.
Ability to independently edit data, run geoprocessing tools, perform basic spatial analysis, and produce maps in ArcGIS Pro.
Understanding of feature classes, tables, joins, relates, coordinate systems, coordinate geometry, and common geospatial data formats.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify inconsistencies in spatial and tabular data.
Ability to investigate routine GIS problems, document findings, and seek guidance when needed.
Strong organizational, communication, and collaboration skills

Preferred Qualifications - What Will Set Them Apart

Experience in forestry, natural resources, utilities, civil engineering, conservation, or other field involving real-world spatial data.
Familiarity with forest-material operations, mobile data collection, or field-to-office workflows.
Experience with ArcGIS Online, hosted feature layers, web maps, Field Maps, GNSS survey equipment, photogrammetry, Survey123, or Dashboards.
Experience with SQL, ETL processes, schema mapping, or data validation.
Exposure to Python or another scripting language.
Familiarity with imagery, remote sensing, parcel data, or environmental datasets.

Working Conditions

This role follows a hybrid schedule. Four days of in-office work per week will be expected during the initial onboarding and integration period, transitioning to a hybrid schedule of 2–3 days in-office per week once sufficiently integrated into the role.

Physical Requirements

Primarily computer-based work requiring extended periods of sitting and/or standing at a computer and typing.
May also include standing, walking, carrying, or lifting (up to 50 lbs.) in support of team tasks.

Travel Requirements

10% or less

This position is not eligible for visa support.

Brief Job Description

The Research Specialist V performs highly advanced (senior-level) research and data dissemination work under minimal supervision, with extensive latitude for the use of independent initiative and judgment. This position designs and implements research and analytical studies; assesses the validity of statistical methods for appropriate application; plans and/or conducts highly advanced research on Medicaid, CHIP; and other agency programs, and applies advanced statistical and/or spatial data analyses techniques to health and human services related data.

Provides consultation and assistance to HHSC staff and other HHS agencies to develop methods and strategies for more effective reporting of data and analyses. Designs, builds, and maintains advanced scripts and code for computer based spatial analysis applications including data acquisition and cleaning. Prepares and presents a variety of reports, studies, and other deliverables containing analyses of health and human services data to agency management, policy analysts, the Legislature, and external customers to provide an understanding of health and human service agencies' programs and issues, including evaluating Managed Care Organizations compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements. Evaluates available spatial datasets and determines which are most appropriate for specific research projects.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular and predictable schedule in accordance with agency leave policy and performs other duties as assigned.

EJF 1: Designs and conducts advanced research and analysis projects specific to Medicaid, CHIP, and other agency programs. Gathers data from multiple sources and performs transformation or pre-analytic processing as required. Ensures location data is accurately geocoded and/or configured for spatial analysis. Types of analyses include spatial distribution of clients, Medicaid providers and licensed practioners, assessing provider network adequacy, evaluating contract compliance, trend and anomaly detection and program change evaluation. (25%)

EJF 2: Works with MCDA Data Management staff to develop and maintain information systems to support ongoing research and analysis. Investigates and validates available reliable data sources, acquires, cleans, and transforms data as needed, reviews, plans and designs research and analyses requiring specialized methods to relate Medicaid/CHIP program and service area objectives to location-based information data and sources. Operates and maintains spatial data systems and programs in Windows and other environments, including evaluation, selection, installation, updates, and upgrades. This includes geocoding, editing, creating, maintaining, displaying, updating, and overlaying a wide variety of data and geographic layers to display the most appropriate and intuitive interpretation of Medicaid/chip related data. Documentation and database management for geospatial purposes are involved. (25%)

EJF 3: Effective professional consultation and collaboration with Medicaid/CHIP division and agency staff and researchers, governmental entities, and other stakeholders for the creation of high-quality research reports, including professional maps. Leads and participates in workgroups to identify the needs in the program areas, and review, develop and design spatial analyses to answer the questions and provide analysis. Communicates effectively with other analysts to share work details, develop plans, devise clear instructions, and formulates cogent inquiries. Presents a variety of graphs, maps, reports, and studies to Medicaid/CHIP staff, agency policy and executive decision makers, the Texas Legislature, and other stakeholders to demonstrate the patterns, trends, and anomalies on provider networks, clients’ services, and program utilization. The information is presented to Medicaid/CHIP leadership and is communicated to stakeholders and managed care organizations to improve program management and service delivery. (20%)

EJF 4: Performs project management functions. Leads and participates in meetings with customers to establish and clarify research and analytical goals, questions, and requirements. Ensures data sources and processes are well documented; that they include accurate technical details for analysts as well as non-technical descriptions appropriate for customers. (20%)

EFJ 5: Evaluates and monitors developments and advancements in GIS and statistical software and recommends the most appropriate software and solutions for research projects and analyses. Designs, develops, implements, and maintains custom-coded applications for data management, cleaning, transformations, and improvements that add efficiencies and accuracy to research and analyses projects. (10%)

Knowledge of advanced research concepts and methodologies.

Knowledge of advanced geospatial analysis and geographic information system concepts and

methods.

Knowledge of cartographic principles, techniques, and procedures.

Knowledge of advanced database management and query methods and systems.

Skill using statistical analysis software such as SAS and R

Skill in programming and scripting languages, such as Python, Visual Basic or PowerShell.

Skill in written and verbal communication for private, public, and professional group interactions.

Skill applying programming techniques to the analysis of large data sets.

Skill in designing, building, implementing and maintain automatic computer processes for data

acquisition, cleaning, transformation, loading and querying.

Skill and experience in the use of Structured Query Language (SQL) and reporting tools.

Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships, set priorities, and manage time

efficiently.

Job Summary

The Environmental Engineering role performs a broader range of environmental engineering tasks related to the analysis, planning, and development of solutions that promote environmental protection, water use sustainability, and responsible water resource management. Working under general supervision of a professional engineer, this role contributes to technical work that improves environmental and public health outcomes across natural and engineered systems. This engineering position addresses environmental and public health protection, mitigation, and prevention of degradation of water, soils, air quality, and habitats. This role may work in one or more diverse areas including water and wastewater treatment and conveyance, stormwater management, solid waste management, hazardous waste management, and related areas. This role conducts analysis, planning, modeling, and design of treatment systems, preparing results, recommendations, plan sets, and other engineering deliverables.

Responsibilities

Perform technical analyses to support identification and evaluation of sustainable water and wastewater management solutions.
Prepare and review technical reports and documentation related to environmental engineering projects.
Assist in the planning and design of environmental protection systems to support public and ecosystem health.
Contribute to facility, watershed, or strategic resource management plans.
Analyze scientific and engineering data and perform quality control checks to support regulatory compliance.
Provide technical support for environmental projects, including modeling of treatment and conveyance systems, vendor coordination, and technical input for permitting and regulatory approvals.
Flexibility to adapt and execute various additional assignments based on evolving needs.

Mentorship

May provide mentorship, guidance, support, and knowledge-sharing to help less experienced team members develop their skills and grow within their roles.

Skills and Competencies

Working knowledge of environmental engineering principles and standard practices.
Developing problem‑solving and analytical skills.
Ability to interpret scientific and engineering data with accuracy and attention to detail.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Experience

Ability to support environmental engineering work involving operational data management, performance monitoring, and evaluation of water, wastewater, recycled water, or advanced treatment facilities.

The University of Oklahoma Health Campus is one of the most comprehensive academic health centers in the nation. Located near the vibrant and growing downtown area of Oklahoma City, it is one of only a few academic medical centers in the nation with seven schools of health in contiguous space (Public Health, Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Allied Health, and Graduate College). Position Overview

This position is responsible for supporting environmental compliance projects across New England, from initiation through completion. This role involves coordinating and participating in stormwater sampling and inspection activities, preparing and implementing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans, performing comprehensive environmental compliance audits, and supporting other project-specific permitting obligations. The role combines technical fieldwork with office responsibilities to ensure that operational practices, documentation, and reporting meet stringent regulatory requirements. This position also supports mentoring junior staff and strengthening the firm’s overall environmental compliance capabilities.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or related field.
6+ years in environmental consulting with demonstrated interest and progression in environmental compliance or permitting.
Strong working knowledge of relevant state-level regulations (New England region) and federal programs.
Experience implementing environmental compliance programs across multiple sites and coordinating with internal staff, vendors, clients, regulators and other stakeholders.
Demonstrated task/project management skills.
Intermediate data evaluation and analytical skills.
Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
Strong documentation and organizational skills.
Experience with common technical protocols and regulatory requirements.
Ability and willingness to support the technical growth of staff level professionals.
OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER preferred.
Experience with EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX) platform (e.g., NetDMR and NetMSGP) preferred.

Essential Duties

Manage, coordinate and/or conduct routine stormwater compliance activities including inspections, sampling and reporting under the EPA’s MSGP and/or other NPDES program requirements, including the evaluation of field data to identify and determine future client needs and project requirements.
Develop, implement and update SWPPPs.
Prepare, maintain and audit SPCC plans.
Conduct routine site inspections to evaluate environmental compliance programs (stormwater, SPCC, air, hazardous waste) and make recommendations to address program deficiencies, as necessary.
Provide project management (scope development, scheduling and budget tracking) for compliance programs, including invoicing and general project administration.
Prepare regulatory reports and other submittals including DMRs.
Conduct regulatory research and permitting for miscellaneous client requests.
Support air permitting evaluations, regulatory research, compliance documentation, and preparation of related permit applications or submittals.
Conduct third-party reviews of permit applications to evaluate adequacy in conformance with local, state, and federal regulations.
Participate in the development of junior staff and work with senior management to continue to grow as a consultant and leader of the firm.

Do you enjoy working across EHS and ESG topics to help shape sustainable outcomes for transactions and post-acquisition strategies? Are you a detail-focused communicator who thrives on fast-paced due diligence work, site visits, and collaborative problem-solving?

If this sounds like you, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our CST Due Diligence UK & Ireland team as our new Principal Environmental Consultant- Due Diligence and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

As a Principal Environmental Consultant for Due Diligence (DD), you will be part of our busy UK transactions team supporting fast-paced UK and global M&A transactions. You will assist with the identification of key EHS and ESG risks and opportunities and provide high-quality, targeted advice to clients on both buy-side and sell-side due diligence projects

Our team advises on transactions across a wide range of sectors, typically including industrial, commercial and infrastructure assets and businesses, often for finance sector clients. We work closely with in-house specialists across several EHS and ESG disciplines to provide targeted due diligence advice. Our clients use this advice to support negotiations during the bidding process and o to make informed impactful decisions on sustainability priorities post-acquisition. 

You will play a key role in the team, principally delivering due diligence assessments, while also supporting project management and the development of client proposals.

Preparation of proposals, including pricing/budgets and timescales. Participation in client discussions and support with developing new client relationships.

Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Job Summary

The Environmental Engineering role performs a broader range of environmental engineering tasks related to the analysis, planning, and development of solutions that promote environmental protection, water use sustainability, and responsible water resource management. Working under general supervision of a professional engineer, this role contributes to technical work that improves environmental and public health outcomes across natural and engineered systems. This engineering position addresses environmental and public health protection, mitigation, and prevention of degradation of water, soils, air quality, and habitats. This role may work in one or more diverse areas including water and wastewater treatment and conveyance, stormwater management, solid waste management, hazardous waste management, and related areas. This role conducts analysis, planning, modeling, and design of treatment systems, preparing results, recommendations, plan sets, and other engineering deliverables.

Responsibilities

Perform technical analyses to support identification and evaluation of sustainable water and wastewater management solutions.
Prepare and review technical reports and documentation related to environmental engineering projects.
Assist in the planning and design of environmental protection systems to support public and ecosystem health.
Contribute to facility, watershed, or strategic resource management plans.
Analyze scientific and engineering data and perform quality control checks to support regulatory compliance.
Provide technical support for environmental projects, including modeling of treatment and conveyance systems, vendor coordination, and technical input for permitting and regulatory approvals.
Flexibility to adapt and execute various additional assignments based on evolving needs.

Mentorship

May provide mentorship, guidance, support, and knowledge-sharing to help less experienced team members develop their skills and grow within their roles.

Skills and Competencies

Working knowledge of environmental engineering principles and standard practices.
Developing problem‑solving and analytical skills.
Ability to interpret scientific and engineering data with accuracy and attention to detail.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Experience

Typically, a minimum of 2 years of related work experience in Environmental Engineering or related field.
Typically certified in the SMS Framework, and progressing through the SMS competencies.

Education

A bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or related field is required.

Preferred Requirements

Ability to support environmental engineering work involving operational data management, performance monitoring, and evaluation of water, wastewater, recycled water, or advanced treatment facilities.
Familiarity with dashboards, visualization tools, historian data, operational records, laboratory results, and other facility datasets used to communicate treatment system performance.
Understanding of key water treatment metrics, including production, recovery, flow, pressure, chemical use, membrane productivity, normalized performance, and related operating trends.
Ability to support advanced water treatment and membrane operational evaluations, including cleaning performance, membrane integrity, fouling assessments, troubleshooting, process optimization, and asset reliability reviews.
Ability to support pilot testing, full-scale facility evaluations, equipment condition assessments, and recommendations for practical operating improvements.
Ability to collaborate with operators, engineers, project managers, and client staff to translate technical findings into reports, calculations, tools, or decision-support deliverables.

Preferred Experience

Experience supporting water, wastewater, recycled water, or advanced treatment projects, including membrane treatment systems such as microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, or reverse osmosis.
Experience compiling, reviewing, or analyzing operational datasets to identify trends, evaluate facility performance, or support engineering recommendations.
Experience developing or supporting dashboards, automated calculations, reports, or visualization tools that reduce manual data processing and improve access to decision-ready information.
Experience supporting membrane system operational evaluations, including review of transmembrane pressure, flux, permeability, recovery, differential pressure, specific flux, cleaning frequency, and production trends.
Experience assisting with troubleshooting of membrane system performance issues, including fouling, scaling, biological activity, chemical cleaning effectiveness, pretreatment impacts, or equipment limitations.
Experience supporting pilot testing, demonstration-scale evaluations, or full-scale optimization studies for advanced treatment systems, including preparation of work plans, sampling plans, data summaries, and technical findings.
Experience preparing technical memoranda, operations support reports, meeting materials, performance summaries, or client-facing recommendations related to treatment process performance and reliability.
Experience coordinating with operations staff or project teams to understand facility workflows, confirm data needs, observe operating practices, and develop tools that support routine monitoring, management reporting, or planning.
Experience supporting membrane replacement planning, asset condition assessments, bench-scale or field testing coordination, vendor coordination, or evaluation of alternative operating strategies.
Experience providing on-site support, field work, or commissioning assistance for treatment facilities, including observations, startup support, performance testing, field data collection, and coordination with operations or construction teams.
Experience supporting secure data transfer, cloud-based data staging, or similar approaches that preserve source-system integrity and align with utility cybersecurity expectations.

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Senior Technical Director, Environmental Scientist
to provide technical and strategic leadership for our Natural Resources Planning and Permitting team in Lawrenceville, New Jersey.

The position will focus on environmental planning and permitting for major New Jersey infrastructure projects. The successful candidate will work closely with WSP’s transportation and infrastructure teams while supporting projects in the electric utility, renewable energy, and oil and gas sectors.

This role is ideal for an established environmental professional who wants to remain technically engaged while leading complex projects, advising clients, developing staff, and growing WSP’s New Jersey permitting practice.

Your Impact

Serve as a senior technical authority for New Jersey environmental planning, natural resource assessment, and permitting.
Develop permitting strategies for transportation, electric transmission and distribution, substations, pipelines, renewable energy, and other infrastructure projects.
Lead regulatory coordination with NJDEP, USACE, USFWS, the New Jersey Pinelands Commission, and other agencies.
Direct wetland, stream, flood hazard, threatened and endangered species, ecological, and environmental constraints assessments.
Review engineering plans and advise project teams on environmental risks, regulatory requirements, avoidance measures, and project schedules.
Oversee preparation of permit applications, environmental reports, agency consultation materials, alternatives analyses, and supporting technical studies.
Serve as Project Director, Project Manager, or senior adviser on complex multidisciplinary assignments.
Lead project strategy, scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk management, and client communication.
Build relationships with transportation agencies, utilities, energy companies, regulatory agencies, and other infrastructure clients.
Lead or support proposals, interviews, client development, and strategic business growth.
Mentor environmental scientists, planners, biologists, and permitting professionals.
Promote technical excellence, collaboration, safety, and consistent quality across projects and offices.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental planning, biology, ecology, natural resources, or a related field.
Extensive progressively responsible experience in environmental consulting, permitting, natural resource planning, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated leadership of complex environmental permitting projects in New Jersey.
Advanced knowledge of New Jersey freshwater wetlands, flood hazard area, coastal, waterfront development, CAFRA, threatened and endangered species, and Pinelands requirements.
Strong working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, Rivers and Harbors Act, Endangered Species Act, and related federal permitting requirements.
Experience coordinating with NJDEP, USACE, USFWS, and other regulatory agencies.
Experience supporting transportation, electric utility, pipeline, oil and gas, renewable energy, or comparable infrastructure projects.
Proven project or program management experience, including responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, quality, and client relationships.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and reviewing complex technical documents.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to travel to client offices, agency meetings, and project sites as needed.
Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a related discipline.
Relevant professional certification, such as PWS, PMP, AICP, or New Jersey Professional Planner.
Established relationships within New Jersey’s transportation, utility, energy, and regulatory communities.
Experience with major transportation programs, electric utility corridors, pipelines, or renewable energy facilities.
Experience with NEPA documentation, public meetings, regulatory hearings, or expert testimony.
Familiarity with GIS-based environmental constraints analysis.

These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OCCUPATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH

The Department of Occupational and Environmental Health at the Hudson College of Public Health, University of Oklahoma Health Campus is hiring a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor.

Environmental And/or Occupational Epidemiology

We are seeking candidates whose work integrates emerging analytic techniques to address one or more of the following focus areas:

Environmental exposures linked to cancer outcomes,
Military and defense-related environmental exposures,
Environmental health concerns of Native American populations and tribes,
Children's environmental health, and/or
Water, food, and air quality impacts on population health.

Required Qualifications

Doctoral degree (Doctor of Philosophy, Doctor of Science, or Doctor of Public Health) in environmental health, industrial hygiene, environmental science, environmental engineering or a closely related field.
Record of publications in peer-reviewed national or international scholarly journals.
Evidence of potential to obtain extramural funding.
For the rank of Associate Professor, a history of external research funding.

Preferences

Established record of teaching at the graduate level
A record of mentoring graduate students, particularly from diverse backgrounds.
Experience in applying emerging analytical techniques (e.g. Big Data, AI, machine learning, geospatial modeling) to public health and environmental data.
Experience working on interdisciplinary or community-engaged research teams.

Application Instructions

Applicants must submit applications through Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/187378.
Applicants are required to provide a CV and cover letter, and three professional references with contact information. For questions about the positions, please contact Misty Wilson at Misty-Wilson@ou.edu.

The ideal candidates meet the required qualifications as an Assistant or Associate Professor and have a documented track record of extramurally funded research. They will contribute to the continued growth and excellence of the department and the university, supporting the University of Oklahoma's strategic plan to lead as a top-tier public research university and to meet AAU-level benchmarks for research, teaching, and service. This individual will contribute to expanding the program across the state with a strong commitment to student-centered values and respect for the student experience.

About Oklahoma City

Oklahoma City is the anchor of a rapidly growing, multicultural metropolitan area with a population of 1.3 million, over 300 days of sunshine annually, very affordable cost of living, excellent schools and a wide array of cultural amenities. The city boasts a strong job market with opportunities in sectors like energy, healthcare, and technology, making it ideal for professionals and families alike. Plus, our revitalized downtown area features arts, entertainment, and local events. To learn more about this impressive city, please take a few minutes to watch this short video.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

The University, in compliance with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations, does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, genetic information, gender identity/expression (consistent with applicable law), age (40 or older), religion, disability, political beliefs, or status as a veteran in any of its policies, practices, or procedures. This includes but is not limited to admissions, employment, housing, financial aid, and educational services.

Why You Belong At The University Of Oklahoma

The University of Oklahoma values our community's unique talents, perspectives, and experiences. At OU, we aspire to harness our innovation, creativity, and collaboration for the advancement of people everywhere. You Belong Here!

About The University Of Oklahoma Health Campus

The University of Oklahoma Health Campus is one of the most comprehensive academic health centers in the nation. Located near the vibrant and growing downtown area of Oklahoma City, it is one of only a few academic medical centers in the nation with seven schools of health in contiguous space (Public Health, Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Allied Health, and Graduate College). It also includes several strategic research centers, institutes, and initiatives to promote research and encourage collaboration among researchers across various disciplines. These include Oklahoma's only National Cancer Institute-Designated Cancer Center, the Stephenson Cancer Center, the Oklahoma Clinical and Translational Science Institute, the Harold Hamm Diabetes Center, the Oklahoma Center for Microbial Pathogenesis, and the Oklahoma Center for Geosciences.

The latest Blue Ridge Institute for Medical Research rankings place OU Health at No. 102 in the nation for funding from the National Institutes of Health - our highest ranking ever. This 27-spot climb over the past two years places OU among the top 3.6% of all 2,838 institutions and entities that receive NIH funding.

Collectively, OU Health Campus researchers received $75.2 million in NIH funding in FY2024, as classified by Blue Ridge.

About The Hudson College Of Public Health

The Hudson College of Public Health, founded in 1967, is Oklahoma's only accredited college of public health and one of just 68 accredited institutions in the U.S. It plays a crucial role in health education and research, offering a top-tier education that prepares students for successful careers in public health practice and research. With a global alumni network spanning all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and 27 countries, and an international student body comprising 10% of the total, the college emphasizes a mission-driven approach to protect and improve health through education, workforce development, research, service, and advocacy.

Located on a vibrant health sciences campus, the Hudson College of Public Health, led by Dr. Dale W. Bratzler, fosters a welcoming culture that values respect and belonging. This environment promotes innovation and collaboration, empowering students to excel in accredited, research-based academic programs with a favorable student-to-faculty ratio.

The college's purpose is to promote healthier tomorrows through education and research today. The Strategic Plan for 2023-2028 emphasizes national recognition in public health research, leading educational and workforce development initiatives, improving health outcomes, and enhancing partnerships to strengthen the impact of its education and services. Through integrated planning and self-studies, the Hudson College of Public Health is committed to continuous improvement and academic excellence in its pursuit of advancing public health.

The Department of Occupational and Environmental Health at the Hudson College of Public Health has been in existence for the past 51 years and has graduated 250 doctoral and master's students. The Department has developed flexible and diversified programs of graduate study, field training, and basic and applied research to accommodate students with a wide range of academic and occupational backgrounds.

Students in the Department seek MS, MPH, and PhD degrees. The industrial hygiene program within the Department has been continuously accredited by ABET since 1994 and continuously supported by a NIOSH-funded training grant since 2004. Faculty are actively developing community engaged research agendas which have led to an EPA-funded Children's Environmental Health Center in U.S. Southern Great Plains and a research contract with the state health department. Faculty members in the Department have received several multi-year grants and contracts from NASA, NSF, CDC, EPA, State Health Department, Oklahoma Department of Commerce, and the Oklahoma Center for the Advancement of Science & Technology (OCAST).

Position Overview

This position is responsible for supporting environmental compliance projects across New England, from initiation through completion. This role involves coordinating and participating in stormwater sampling and inspection activities, preparing and implementing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans, performing comprehensive environmental compliance audits, and supporting other project-specific permitting obligations. The role combines technical fieldwork with office responsibilities to ensure that operational practices, documentation, and reporting meet stringent regulatory requirements. This position also supports mentoring junior staff and strengthening the firm’s overall environmental compliance capabilities.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or related field.
6+ years in environmental consulting with demonstrated interest and progression in environmental compliance or permitting.
Strong working knowledge of relevant state-level regulations (New England region) and federal programs.
Experience implementing environmental compliance programs across multiple sites and coordinating with internal staff, vendors, clients, regulators and other stakeholders.
Demonstrated task/project management skills.
Intermediate data evaluation and analytical skills.
Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
Strong documentation and organizational skills.
Experience with common technical protocols and regulatory requirements.
Ability and willingness to support the technical growth of staff level professionals.
OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER preferred.
Experience with EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX) platform (e.g., NetDMR and NetMSGP) preferred.

Essential Duties

Manage, coordinate and/or conduct routine stormwater compliance activities including inspections, sampling and reporting under the EPA’s MSGP and/or other NPDES program requirements, including the evaluation of field data to identify and determine future client needs and project requirements.
Develop, implement and update SWPPPs.
Prepare, maintain and audit SPCC plans.
Conduct routine site inspections to evaluate environmental compliance programs (stormwater, SPCC, air, hazardous waste) and make recommendations to address program deficiencies, as necessary.
Provide project management (scope development, scheduling and budget tracking) for compliance programs, including invoicing and general project administration.
Prepare regulatory reports and other submittals including DMRs.
Conduct regulatory research and permitting for miscellaneous client requests.
Support air permitting evaluations, regulatory research, compliance documentation, and preparation of related permit applications or submittals.
Conduct third-party reviews of permit applications to evaluate adequacy in conformance with local, state, and federal regulations.
Participate in the development of junior staff and work with senior management to continue to grow as a consultant and leader of the firm.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position works in the field as well as the office environment. In the field, candidate will be working independently or leading a larger team at exterior project sites to perform compliance audits, sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and potentially oversight of subcontractors. These field activities require the ability to drive to different project sites and physically move around outdoors in various terrains, in adverse weather conditions and occasionally for extended or irregular hours. Conducting work involves the use of hand-held monitoring instruments and tools, as well as water sampling equipment, which requires the ability to routinely lift and carry objects, stand, walk, reach, bend, squat, kneel and twist. Office work is primarily stationary/sedentary using a computer and keyboard/mouse requiring repetitive hand movements.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you an experienced environmental due diligence consultant, skilled in uncovering environmental risks and turning technical findings into clear, actionable advice for decision-makers? Do you enjoy working across EHS and ESG topics to help shape sustainable outcomes for transactions and post-acquisition strategies? Are you a detail-focused communicator who thrives on fast-paced due diligence work, site visits, and collaborative problem-solving?

If this sounds like you, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our CST Due Diligence UK & Ireland team as our new Principal Environmental Consultant- Due Diligence and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

As a Principal Environmental Consultant for Due Diligence (DD), you will be part of our busy UK transactions team supporting fast-paced UK and global M&A transactions. You will assist with the identification of key EHS and ESG risks and opportunities and provide high-quality, targeted advice to clients on both buy-side and sell-side due diligence projects

Our team advises on transactions across a wide range of sectors, typically including industrial, commercial and infrastructure assets and businesses, often for finance sector clients. We work closely with in-house specialists across several EHS and ESG disciplines to provide targeted due diligence advice. Our clients use this advice to support negotiations during the bidding process and o to make informed impactful decisions on sustainability priorities post-acquisition. 

You will play a key role in the team, principally delivering due diligence assessments, while also supporting project management and the development of client proposals. 

Your key responsibilities will be:

Preparation of proposals, including pricing/budgets and timescales. Participation in client discussions and support with developing new client relationships.
Project Management and coordination of medium to large projects including multi-site projects over several geographies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence.
Delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Limited Environmental Compliance Review(LECR) assessments for a range of sites, including more complex manufacturing facilities; including participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing focussed client reports. 
Delivery of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) assessments of companies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence. This will include desk-based research (review of data rooms and publicly available information), participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing client focussed reports.

About You

If you have relevant EHS/ESG knowledge, experience in due diligence and want to advance your career in a collaborative team, we would like to hear from you.What matters most to us:

Relevant degree/qualifications. Ideally in environmental studies/geography or similar.
Sound understanding of UK environmental regulations and an understanding of key environmental and sustainability regulations in Europe.
7 to 12 years of practical work experience in other companies where you have personally been involved in the delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, LECR assessments, ideally including to ASTM standards, and ideally also ESG assessments. Have the ability to understand information quickly and work efficiently, proactively and autonomously.
Experience in supporting the preparation of proposals.  
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), and be comfortable engaging with external clients and advisors.
Project Management experience.
A collaborative approach and willingness to travel, typically within the UK and Ireland.

What We Can Offer You

Commitment to your development
Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
Flexible work environment
27 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Matched pension contributions
Private medical cover and life assurance

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application and CV online. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture.
